main_text.p: sese polluat, de dote item prospicere herus debeat, lib.i.cap.9. exposita est, & in legibus præcepti hu-jus superiori cap. breviter repetita.
Liberæ virgines, aut indigenæ fuerunt, aut ex-tranæ vel gentiles.
Indigenæ iterum, aut integræ, parentibus ve-rò orbatæ, & proprios fundos habentes fuerunt; aut corruptæ.

Illis extra tribum suam nubere fas non fuit, ne hæreditates de tribu aliâ[?] in aliam transferren-tur. Cujus rei causam lib.i.cap.8. assignavimus. Has, qui corruperat, honesto & casto conjugio sibi copulare tenebatur. Cujus legis rationem & æquitatem lib.i.cap.10. demonstravimus.

Additur tamen legi huic exceptio, si pater corruptæ, stupratori dare illam conjugem re-nuat. Quæ restrictio consensum & authoritatem parentum, liberorum desponsationibus ac-cedere & intervenire oportere docet. Id quod De parentum consensu & authoritate in liberorum desponsationibus.plurima etiam alia sacrarum literarum exempla, honestis & æquis rationibus nixa, confirmant. Abrahamus enim suâ authoritate Isaaci desponsationem gubernat, omniaque ad hanc rem necessaria constituit & moderatur, Gen.24. Isaacus Jacobum in Mesopotamiam mittit, hoc consilio, ut inde sibi uxorem accipiat, Gen.28.v.1.2. Simson, visâ muliere Philistæâ, quæ ipsi placebat, non suopte arbitrio, insciis aut invitis parentibus, illam ducit, sed parentes rogat, ut eam ipsi in uxorem accipiant, Judic.14. vers.2. page.notes: The left strip shows the edge of the neighbouring page and was left out. Uncertain readings: "aliâ" (possibly plain "alia") and "Philistæâ". The running head is set in italic and small capitals and is given as printed. No marginal reference marks appear in the text. Printed "eft" was read as "est" and long s is rendered as plain s throughout. The Roman numeral written with a dotted-less i ("lib.ı.cap") was read as "i".
